long_biography.plain_text:
Trained in business administration at Bocconi University, Luca Rovati entered his family's pharmaceutical group in 1986 as a financial executive. He later became chief executive, using acquisitions of Laboratori Guieu, Biochimici PSN and Germany's Madaus Pharma to broaden Rottapharm from its research roots into a larger European consumer-healthcare business.

The decisive transaction came in 2014, when Rovati negotiated the sale of Rottapharm to Meda for €2.275 billion in cash, shares and deferred consideration. The family became Meda's second-largest shareholder, and Rovati served as deputy chairman. He subsequently shifted toward investment management through Fidim and co-founded the private-equity firm Armonia SGR.
